saints.name: Sts. Paul Miki and Companions
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The twenty-six martyrs crucified on a hill above Nagasaki, first fruits of the Church in Japan, who died forgiving their persecutors…
biography: Paul Miki was born about 1564 into a Japanese family of the samurai class and entered the Society of Jesus, where he became a preacher of rare gifts. When the ruler Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who in 1587 had decreed the banishment of all missionaries, turned against the Church, Paul Miki was seized with twenty-five companions — three Jesuits, six Franciscans, and seventeen Japanese laymen, among them three boys.

Condemned to die at Nagasaki, they were marched through the winter from Kyoto and Osaka to the place of execution, and on 5 February 1597 were crucified on the hill of Nishizaka above the city and pierced with lances. From his cross Paul Miki declared that he was dying as a Christian, forgave his executioners, and preached Christ to the onlookers.

The twenty-six were beatified in 1627 by Pope Urban VIII and canonized on 8 June 1862 by Pope Pius IX, the first fruits of the Church in Japan. As the protomartyrs of that nation they are honoured as patrons of Japan.
saints.knownFor: The witness of the twenty-six protomartyrs of Japan.
